Reactor System Inspection

Light water reactors (LWRs) represent the dominant global nuclear technology, with both pressurized water reactor (PWR) and boiling water reactor (BWR) variants operating under different thermal and pressure conditions. Both designs require comprehensive NDT programs addressing reactor vessel integrity, primary system piping, and auxiliary component assessment. Boiling water reactors operate at lower pressure but experience higher neutron fluence and more aggressive water chemistry, creating different embrittlement and corrosion challenges.

Advanced reactor designs including heavy-water reactors, graphite-moderated designs, and experimental fast reactors operate under conditions distinct from commercial LWRs, requiring specialized inspection approaches. NDT training programs address reactor-type-specific requirements, enabling inspectors and engineers to understand design differences and their implications for defect mechanisms and inspection methodologies.

Spent fuel pool infrastructure requires inspection to verify structural integrity of racks, cooling systems, and fuel cladding condition. NDT consulting services experienced with nuclear decommissioning and extended storage address challenges unique to aging fuel and storage infrastructure. Integrated approaches combining ultrasonic inspection, borescopic examination, and visual assessment establish baseline conditions and predict continued safe operation.

Containment structures, whether steel-lined concrete (PWR) or steel shells (BWR), require periodic inspection to verify pressure boundary integrity. Radiographic examination of containment welds combined with visual inspection for corrosion and cracking establishes aging assessment baselines. Digital twin solutions integrate aging assessment data across multiple inspection campaigns, supporting license renewal decisions and extended operation planning.

Comprehensive facility inspection programs addressing all critical systems and structures ensure that reactor operations continue safely throughout extended operating licenses, demonstrating society's commitment to nuclear energy's safe utilization.
